solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Kiss chap bringing round goat milk vat, suggest cuddles

indicators.note: bringing something round turns it about, so the string taken from the phrase is read from right to left
the phrase goat milk vat suggest holds a run of letters in its embrace, so a string is lifted from inside it

explanation.surface: A man brings a goat's milk vat round and hints that a hug might follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuddles' picks out TMILKVATSUG from inside the words, and 'bringing round' reverses it. The definition is cryptic: the Kiss is the famous gold-leaf painting, so its 'chap' is the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kiss is the best-known painting of the Austrian Secession artist, so the man behind it is its painter.

clue.text: If admitted to grand doorway, smarten up!

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: admitted to means the word if is let in, placed inside the other letters

parts.note: an entry is a way in, such as a doorway

explanation.surface: An order to tidy yourself up if you're let through a grand entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To gentrify an area is to renovate and upgrade it to suit wealthier residents, so to spruce it up.

clue.text: The lot — from gypsum to talcum

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run gypsum to talcum

explanation.surface: Everything, ranging from one mineral powder to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand total of everything added together is the whole amount, the entire lot.

clue.text: Cancel yearbook; second article's missing

indicators.note: missing means that letter is absent from the yearbook word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
a is the indefinite article, and second points to the latter A of the yearbook word

explanation.surface: A publisher scraps the yearbook because its second piece has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to declare it void, to cancel it.

clue.text: Our cake mix, an inspiration to Bob Dylan

indicators.note: a cake mix is stirred together, so the letters of our cake are jumbled

explanation.surface: A home baking mix somehow inspired a famous songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Kerouac, the Beat Generation novelist of On the Road, was a major influence on Dylan.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan has said that the Beat novelist's writing shaped his own, so the author was one of his inspirations.

clue.text: This month, Yankee left Spain going first class!

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means of this month in old business letters
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: An American departs for Spain this month, travelling first class.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, used in old commercial letters ('your letter of the 5th inst.'), means of the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in style means doing it lavishly and elegantly, as a first-class traveller would.

clue.text: The residents know lofts should be renovated

indicators.note: renovated means remade, so the letters of know lofts are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The local people are well aware their attic rooms need doing up.
explanation.definitionFit: The people who live in a town are its residents, its inhabitants.

clue.text: Boy infiltrating Al-Qaeda, off and on

indicators.note: off and on means every other letter of Al-Qaeda is kept, skipping those between

explanation.surface: A young man goes undercover inside a terrorist group, on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is an everyday word for a boy or young male.

clue.text: I'd titter — LOL! Funny! — about opening of romantic novel

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the initial letter
funny means odd, so the letters of I'd titter LOL are put in a peculiar order
opening of points to the first letter of romantic

explanation.surface: A reader laughs out loud at the first page of a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges I'D TITTER LOL into LITTLEDORIT, and 'about' wraps it round R, the opening of 'romantic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Dorrit is a novel by Charles Dickens about a girl raised in the Marshalsea debtors' prison.

clue.text: See 7
New bill of fare promoting uniform spirit of Rome

indicators.note: promoting moves something up the order, so the letter for uniform is shifted to the front of the menu word

parts.note: a bill of fare is a restaurant's menu
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A restaurant's new menu pushes a set dress code, oddly tied to a Roman ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' looks like the menu advertising something; it actually means moving the uniform letter to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Roman religion a numen is the divine power or presiding spirit dwelling in a place or thing.

clue.text: Fragrant liquid making rower's tea

indicators.note: making here means fashioning something new out of the letters of rower's tea, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A scented drink is brewed for an oarsman's afternoon cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: Water distilled with rose petals is a perfumed liquid used in cooking and cosmetics.

clue.text: Fauvist sculpture of Our Lady grabs Uffizi's leaders

indicators.note: grabs means the remoulded letters seize and hold the gallery's opening letters inside them
a sculpture shapes material into a new form, so the letters of Our Lady are remoulded
leaders are the front letters, here the opening pair of the gallery name Uffizi

explanation.surface: A statue of the Virgin Mary seizes the attention of the heads of Florence's great gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpture of' rearranges OUR LADY into RAOULDY, and 'grabs' puts UF, the first two letters of Uffizi, inside it. The Uffizi is the famous art gallery in Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: Raoul Dufy was a French painter associated with Fauvism, the movement of bold, unnatural colour led by Matisse.

clue.text: Very large tenor, international household name in opera

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
T is a standard abbreviation for tenor in choral scores

explanation.surface: A hefty international tenor has become a celebrity in the opera world.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a famous singer, but the name belongs to a conductor, Sir Georg Solti, long music director at Covent Garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Solti was a world-famous conductor of opera, celebrated for the first studio recording of Wagner's Ring cycle.

clue.text: Swiss currency note carried when desperate

indicators.note: carried means the currency word bears the note within it

parts.note: the franc is the currency of Switzerland
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt te

explanation.surface: A Swiss banknote is taken along at a moment of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests the banknote of the surface, but here it is a musical note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic describes someone wild with worry or haste, much like a person in a desperate state.

clue.text: Mild paint mixture to go on walls of temple

indicators.note: to go on, in a down entry, means the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: tempera is paint made by mixing pigment with egg yolk

indicators.note: walls of means only the outermost letters of temple are used

explanation.surface: A gentle painting job: daub egg-based paint on a church's walls.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is the first and last letters of 'temple'.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperate climate is free from extremes, so it is gentle and moderate.

clue.text: Aphrodite's Child resentful in retirement

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word for resentful is read in reverse

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or resentful, as in feeling sore about a slight

explanation.surface: A band, or a son, nursing a grudge after stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: Aphrodite's Child was also a Greek rock band, which gives the surface its musical colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the god of love is the son of the goddess of love, Aphrodite.

clue.text: Father Euan probed by senior detective's analytical technique

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; here it stands, as in a Freudian slip, for the method of psychoanalysis

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: probed by means Euan has the detective's letters pushed inside him

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a senior police rank

explanation.surface: A priest named Euan is quizzed by a top policeman using his interrogation method.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is an adjective, standing for the psychoanalytic method it names.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysis, the method of analysing the unconscious devised by Sigmund Freud, is named after him.

clue.text: Sound horn entering Wash — turbulent wave pattern

indicators.note: entering means the horn sound goes inside the scrambled letters
turbulent waters are churned up, so the letters of Wash are scrambled

parts.note: to toot is to sound a horn

explanation.surface: A foghorn blares across the choppy Wash, with its waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a broad bay on England's east coast; 'turbulent' gives SAWH from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawtooth wave rises steadily then drops sharply, a jagged waveform shaped like a saw's teeth.

clue.text: Discovering instant warning

indicators.note: dis-covering means stripping off the cover, so the outer letters of the word for instant are removed

parts.note: a moment is an instant, a very short time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovering' is read as dis-covering: take the outer M and T off MOMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign foretelling something, often bad, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Writer upset very old king over boycott

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, so in a down entry the whole string is read bottom to top

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
to ban something is to boycott it

explanation.surface: An author is distressed that an elderly monarch has backed a boycott.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses VOKOBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Following German approval, Ford secures 28 capital

indicators.note: following means the car-and-skill part comes after the German yes

parts.note: ja is German for yes

indicators.note: secures means the car name holds the other answer fast inside it

parts.note: the Ka is a small Ford car model
the answer to 28 across, a word meaning skill

explanation.surface: Once Germany gives the nod, a Ford grabs another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ka is a small Ford hatchback; '28' means the answer to 28 across, used as letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Jakarta is the capital city of Indonesia, on the island of Java.

clue.text: Texan oilman acquiring uranium mine beginning to endanger planet

indicators.note: acquiring means the oilman's initials take in the other letters between them

parts.note: J.R. Ewing was the scheming oil baron of the TV soap Dallas
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
a pit is a mine, especially a coal mine

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of endanger

explanation.surface: An oil tycoon buys a uranium mine that could threaten the world.
explanation.walkthrough: J.R. Ewing, villain of the American TV soap Dallas, is the crossword's stock Texan oilman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, fifth from the Sun.

clue.text: Nine running amok in Virginia city

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters sit inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: running amok means going wild, so the letters of nine are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Nine people go on a rampage in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia city' looks like the definition, but Virginia only gives letters and the city is the Austrian capital. 'running amok' gives IENN.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria, on the Danube.

clue.text: Get the better of old upper-class idiot

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage, as in U and non-U speech
a twit is a silly person, an idiot

explanation.surface: Beating a foolish old aristocrat at his own game.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to get the upper hand over them by being cleverer.

clue.text: Wearing American couture, at last engaged!

parts.note: to be in a garment is to be wearing it
US is short for American, as in the US

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of couture

explanation.surface: A bride in American designer fashion finally announces her engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone or room that is in use is occupied, so it is engaged.

clue.text: Bit on the side came via professional channel

parts.note: by means via, as in travel by train
pro is short for professional
a duct is a channel or tube carrying fluid

explanation.surface: A lover on the side arrived through a work contact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit on the side' suggests an affair, but it is a secondary product made alongside the main one.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary product arising in making something else is incidental, a bit produced on the side.

clue.text: It's extracted from poppy in US –- my failing, occasionally

definitions.text: It's extracted from poppy in US –- my failing, occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of poppy in US my is kept

explanation.surface: A confession: an occasional weakness for a drug drawn from American poppies.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters taken alternately from 'poppy in US my' spell the drug, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: The narcotic drug is made from the dried latex of the opium poppy's seed pods.

clue.text: Pioneering sales rep targets this Suffolk town

parts.note: something pioneering is new, never done before
the people a sales rep aims at form a market

explanation.surface: A trail-blazing salesman sets his sights on this East Anglian town.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWMARKET is a Suffolk town, the home of British horse racing; the clue can also be read whole as a playful description of a fresh market.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a town in the English county of Suffolk, famous for its racecourse and stud farms.

clue.text: Jones is blue, taking day off

indicators.note: taking ... off says a piece is removed from the colour word
off completes taking off, telling the solver to remove the letter for day

parts.note: indigo is a deep blue colour

explanation.surface: Someone surnamed Jones feels down and takes a day's leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones was the English architect of the Banqueting House in Whitehall.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo Jones, the seventeenth-century architect and stage designer, is the classic first name for this surname.

clue.text: Advanced right skill

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean a craft or knack, as in the art of conversation.

clue.text: Dave crashed by Route 1 out of German city — I'll never forget his scream

indicators.note: by places the road letters beside the shuffled name
crashed means Dave is smashed up and his letters rearranged

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a route

indicators.note: out of means the letter for one is dropped from the city name

parts.note: Munich is the Bavarian capital
the figure 1 looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: Dave's car crash on the road out of a German city left an unforgettable scream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' turns DAVE into EDVA; 'out of' drops the I (1) from MUNICH to give MUNCH. The definition plays on The Scream, the painter's best-known work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian artist painted The Scream, so his scream is the one no gallery visitor forgets.
